source_evidence.finding: Changing lacp_enabled marks setting_changed; default action_script is reboot. Only policy-only changes take restart_net_and_phy.
lacp_enabled belongs to FT_LINK_AGGREGATION; its service mapping is REBOOT.
Existing net_and_phy dispatcher stops network services and LAN, then calls config_lacp and starts LAN/services; not yet tested as an enable/disable replacement on this board.
Archived BE98 page also uses reboot for LACP enable/disable and network restart for policy-only changes; this audit does not establish when the behavior was introduced.

interpretation.verified: Both observed reboots were explicitly requested by userspace services. The page hash matches the unchanged stock firmware userspace.
interpretation.cfgsync_inference: Superseded: the master own lacp_enabled=0 does not establish the value it manages for a particular node. AiMesh UI provides per-node LACP via config_changed with re_mac. A second reboot did disable bonding, but the exact config payload and origin were not captured. Later cfg_client requested another reboot, after which node LACP was enabled while master own LACP remained 0.
interpretation.fallback: Returning to original slot 2 follows the intentionally uncommitted one-time trial policy; no permanent boot-slot change was made during this diagnosis.

repair_requirements: Establish correct per-node configuration ownership and source of each update; do not assume the controller own LACP setting should match the node. Existing UI uses per-node config_changed/re_mac.
Route only validated LAN aggregation changes to a network reconfiguration action; retain real reboots for independent settings that require them.
Update both UI action selection and cfgsync feature handling; changing only the UI does not prevent the second reboot.
Verify bond create/remove, bridge membership, Broadcom acceleration, AiMesh reconnection and AI-board access; assert boot ID unchanged during apply.
The existing restart_net_and_phy action still interrupts LAN/Wi-Fi/services and is not equivalent to a zero-disruption bond-only update.
Keep any userspace repair separate from the kernel-only firmware baseline.
changes_performed: Read-only router/CCR diagnostics plus local source extraction and reports. No nvram set/commit, service restart, flash, reboot, firmware commitment or device file modification.

followup_comparison.user_observation: User reports both LACP enable/disable and other settings did not generally require whole-device reboot on BE98 and prior AXE16000. Do not reinterpret this as policy-only changes.
followup_comparison.be98_live: Kernel #36, PID1 systemd, sw_mode=3, re_mode=0, cfg_master=1, lacp_enabled=0, uptime >20 hours
followup_comparison.be19000ai_live: Kernel #1, PID1 rc, sw_mode=3, re_mode=1, cfg_master=0, lacp_enabled=1 after additional reboot

be98.behavior: LACP enabled value change marks setting_changed; default reboot retained for Broadcom path. Policy-only change chooses restart_net_and_phy.

be19000ai.behavior: LACP enabled value change marks setting_changed; default reboot retained for Broadcom path. Policy-only change chooses restart_net_and_phy.

followup_comparison.systemd_semantics: Existing BE98 rc init loop sees g_reboot after handle_notifications and enters SIGTERM path; rc-client and broker forward reboot to systemctl reboot. No general suppression or conversion of reboot into network restart found.
followup_comparison.axe16000_historical_evidence: 2026-09-17 result.json confirms service restart_wireless recovered radios without whole-device reboot. This is not a recorded LACP toggle test.
followup_comparison.per_node_lacp: aimesh/aimesh_topology.html:3150-3153 builds data.lacp_enabled, sends to manage_set_config(data,node.mac); lines4698-4720 read node.config.link_aggregation and submit action_mode=config_changed with re_mac.
followup_comparison.remaining_gap: No contemporaneous request/action trace of BE98 or AXE16000 LACP enable/disable without reboot. Static page defaults alone cannot explain the reported difference.
followup_comparison.mutations: Local report updates only. No router settings or services changed.
